# Decision-threshold cost analysis

Cost model: FP (good order held/manual review) = 1.0 unit, FN (RTO missed, ships anyway) = 12.0 units (industry: RTO loss + reverse logistics ~10-15x review cost; methodology per
Drummond & Holte, *Machine Learning* 65:95-130, 2006 - see docs/research/INDEX.md).

## 3-way threshold sweep (Track C — Bahnsen BMR Eq.(5) with constant `c_fn=600`)

| threshold | flagged | precision | recall | FP | FN | total cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.15 | 663 | 0.406 | 0.789 | 394 | 72 | 1258.0 |
| 0.2 | 571 | 0.443 | 0.742 | 318 | 88 | 1374.0 |
| 0.25 | 505 | 0.465 | 0.689 | 270 | 106 | 1542.0 |
| 0.3 | 447 | 0.485 | 0.636 | 230 | 124 | 1718.0 |
| 0.35 | 393 | 0.506 | 0.584 | 194 | 142 | 1898.0 |
| 0.4 | 338 | 0.533 | 0.528 | 158 | 161 | 2090.0 |
| 0.5 | 229 | 0.581 | 0.39 | 96 | 208 | 2592.0 |
| 0.6 | 146 | 0.651 | 0.279 | 51 | 246 | 3003.0 |

**Cost-optimal threshold: 0.15** (cost 1258.0 units)

## V3 §11.6 5-way intervention policy (Track N — Bahnsen BMR Eq.(5) per-amount FN cost)

Track N extends Track C's 3-way `optimal_decision()` to the full V3 §11.6
intervention set: `{ship, otp_verify, partial_cod, address_check, hold}`.
Per Bahnsen 2013 BMR Eq.(5), the FN cost is the **per-transaction order amount**
(NOT a constant — the headline of the Bahnsen paper). Per-intervention
effectiveness rates are taken from the Pragma 2025 RTO-mitigation benchmark
(OTP 0.78–0.84, partial COD 0.60–0.70, address check 0.42–0.48); conservative
point estimates are used.

### Per-intervention cost model

| Intervention | Cost formula (INR) | Default weights |
|---|---|---|
| `ship`         | `p · amount`                                              | — (baseline) |
| `otp_verify`   | `c_otp + (1 − eff_otp) · p · amount`                      | c_otp=5, eff=0.82 |
| `partial_cod`  | `c_partial_cod + (1 − eff_cod) · p · amount`             | c_partial_cod=10, eff=0.65 |
| `address_check`| `c_address_check + (1 − eff_addr) · p · amount`         | c_address_check=3, eff=0.45 |
| `hold`         | `c_hold + residual_ship_rate · p · amount`               | c_hold=20, residual=0.30 |

The cost-optimal intervention is `argmin` over the five. The recommendation
is surfaced in `POST /risk/score`'s `intervention` + `intervention_costs`
fields and in `GET /v1/policy/cost-curves`'s `intervention_curves` +
`intervention_crossover` fields.

### Cost-optimal intervention by probability × amount bracket

The table below shows the cost-optimal intervention at each
probability threshold × order-amount bracket, computed by
`optimal_intervention(p, amount_inr)` with default weights. The ship→otp_verify
crossover is at `p·amount ≈ c_otp / eff_otp = 5 / 0.82 ≈ 6.10 INR`; below
that boundary the OTP fee exceeds the residual RTO loss, so `ship` (baseline)
wins; above it, `otp_verify` dominates the "soft" interventions because its
effectiveness (0.82) is higher than partial COD (0.65), address check (0.45),
or hold's residual ship rate (0.30 → effective RTO reduction 0.70).

| amount (INR) ↓ \ p → | 0.05 | 0.10 | 0.15 | 0.20 | 0.30 | 0.40 | 0.50 | 0.70 | 0.85 | 0.95 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100    | ship | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify |
| 1,000  | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify |
| 5,000  | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify |
| 12,400 | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify |
| 25,000 | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify |
| 52,000 | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify |
| 100,000 | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify | otp_verify |

**Default-weight crossover: `ship` → `otp_verify` at `p · amount ≈ 6.10 INR`.**
Above that boundary, `otp_verify` dominates across the full sweep — the
cost-model's truthful answer with the published Pragma 2025 effectiveness
rates is "send an OTP, it's cheap and effective".

### Re-tuning the weights changes the cost-optimal intervention

The 5-way cost model is parameterised by `DEFAULT_INTERVENTION_WEIGHTS` (and
overridable per-call via the `weights` arg). Different markets / operational
contexts re-tune the crossovers:

| Market context | Re-tuned weights | Cost-optimal intervention at p=0.9, amt=₹52,000 |
|---|---|---|
| Default (Pragma 2025)         | `c_hold=20, residual=0.30`                | `otp_verify` (₹8429 vs hold ₹14060) |
| Cheap manual review (high-touch ops team that blocks 99% of held orders) | `c_hold=1, residual=0.01` | `hold` (₹469 vs otp_verify ₹8429) |
| Expensive OTP (no SMS gateway, IVR-only) | `c_otp=1000, eff_otp=0.0` | `hold` (₹1508 vs otp_verify ₹5960) |

This is the BMR-vs-execution gap Bahnsen 2013 closes: the cost-optimizer
recommends the intervention with the lowest *expected* monetary cost, not
the intervention with the highest *recall* — and the recommendation changes
with the local cost structure. The operator can override the weights at
call time (the `intervention_weights` field in the `/risk/score` response
exposes the weights actually used so the recommendation's provenance is
auditable).

### Reference papers

- Bahnsen, Stojanovic, Aouada, Ottersten — *Cost Sensitive Credit Card Fraud
  Detection using Bayes Minimum Risk*, ICMLA 2013, DOI 10.1109/ICMLA.2013.68.
  Eq.(5): per-transaction FN cost = `amount_inr` (not constant). The
  headline of the paper.
- Drummond & Holte — *Cost Curves: An Improved Method for Visualizing
  Classifier Performance*, Machine Learning 65:95-130, 2006,
  DOI 10.1007/s10994-006-8199-5. `find_model_crossover` capability adapted
  to the 5-way intervention sweep → `intervention_crossover`.
- Pragma 2025 RTO-mitigation benchmark (OTP 0.78–0.84, partial COD
  0.60–0.70, address check 0.42–0.48 — see `docs/research/INDEX.md`).
